answer: Sybil resistance comes from slashable stake bonds. Before the economy counts an agent, that identity must lock its own collateral; to forge a hundred fake agents an attacker must post a hundred deposits. Cost scales linearly with the number of Sybils, and proven fraud burns the bond outright. A bot farm minting quartz or chasing a nectar reward risks losing more stake than it can steal, so a copy that looks free is actually expensive. Honest agents keep their weight because inflating headcount demands real, forfeitable capital, not a fresh key.
